newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh police rescue 16 boys, arrest two men.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh police rescue 16 boys, arrest two men.

text.p: Bangladesh police rescued 16 boys from a house in capital Dhaka, and arrested two men suspected of trafficking in children, newspapers and police said on Monday.
The Bangla-language daily Bhorer Kagoj said police, in a midnight raid on Saturday, stormed a house in Dhaka's Banani residential area and found the boys huddled in a dark locked room.

The newspaper said the police suspected that the children, aged between six and nine, had been waiting to be smuggled out of the country. They were taken to the local Gulshan police station for safe custody.
Police officials were quoted as saying the children had been brought to Dhaka by bus on Saturday from four different villages in the district of Comilla, some 100 km (60 miles) from Dhaka.
Police said they were interrogating the suspects and looking for the parents of the children.
The arrested men told the police they were taking the children to an orphanage in the northern district of Tangail where they would be given free lodging, food and education.
In December, police in Chittagong port city raided a madrasa (Moslem religious school) and rescued 24 children who had been chained by their teachers for months.
"Minor boys and girls are falling in various traps, and many go missing for ever," one police officer said on Monday. "This is a matter of serious concern," he said.
Local human rights bodies say at least 15,000 people, mostly women and children, are smuggled out of Bangladesh by traffickers every year.
The women mostly end up in brothels in neighbouring countries while the fate of many children, some as young as three years, remained a mystery.
Police believe a large number of smuggled boys are used as jockeys in camel races in the Middle East and Gulf states.
